prev_agent: No, there is no Problem Formulation section in the appendix. The appendix has 16 `\section` headings (§A–§P), and none is titled "Problem Setup", "Problem Formulation", "Notation", or "Preliminaries". Concretely: | Appendix § | Title | Scope | |---|---|---| | §A | Experimental Setup Details | Backbone *implementation* specs, training hyperparams, per-baseline configs, RR-MoA pseudocode | | §B | Deployment-Regime Motivation | Why frozen-adapter regime matters (multi-tenant, on-device, cross-task) | | §D | Proposition Proofs | Math definitions for the proofs (M, Σ, S, R(D)) — only as needed for theorems | The closest candidate is **§A Experimental Setup Details**, but that is correctly scoped as *experimental* setup (which Adam learning rate, which seeds, which encoder blocks per backbone) — i.e., implementation choices, not problem definition. The new §3 `\textbf{Problem setup.}` and §A are complementary, not overlapping: - **§3 Problem Setup** (body): defines what we're solving — input/output spaces ($\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times c}$, $\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{h\times c}$), the frozen-feature-extractor regime ($\nabla_\theta\equiv 0$), the parameter budget ($|\phi|\leq 500$K), the mixture-of-adapters formalism, and the training objective. - **§A Experimental Setup** (appendix): specifies *how* we instantiate it — Adam $\eta{=}10^{-3}$, batch 128, 15 epochs, seeds {42,…,46}, per-backbone block counts, per-baseline configurations. So nothing was accidentally relegated. The body now has a proper Problem Setup, and the appendix has the experimental config that supports it — the conventional NeurIPS split. Two minor potential overlaps worth flagging (both small enough to leave as-is): - §3 mentions $T{=}512$; §A also implies it via "MOMENT-small ($d{=}512$, 8 encoder blocks…)" but doesn't explicitly restate $T$. - §3 mentions horizons $h\in\{96,192,336,720\}$; §C "Multi-Horizon Evaluation" uses the same set but in the context of the multi-horizon table rather than as a problem-spec restatement.
